title: Walking for weight loss: how many steps a day?
intro: No need to chase 10,000 steps straight away. Start by adding 1,000 to 2,000 steps to your current average, and aim for an estimated 7,000 to 10,000 steps a day step by step.
muscles: Legs, glutes, calves and core, plus heart health. Walking adds to your daily energy burn, but weight loss still depends on eating too.
steps: Check your average daily steps for a week using your phone or watch.
Add 1,000 steps a day to that average. Increase again every 1-2 weeks.
Walk for 10 minutes after meals, for example after lunch at the mamak.
Park further away, take the stairs, and walk while you're on the phone.
Once in a while, walk fast enough that you can talk but can't sing.
mistakes: Jumping straight from 3,000 to 12,000 steps and ending up with sore feet or giving up.
Feeling like you've walked a lot, so you eat bigger portions or drink more sweet drinks than usual.
Wearing unsuitable footwear like thin slippers for long walks.
easier: Break it into 3-4 short walks of 5-10 minutes throughout the day.
harder: Add hills or stairs, walk faster, or do a 30-45 minute walk at the park on weekends.
dose: Start with your current average plus 1,000 steps. Beginner target: an estimated 7,000-8,000 steps a day, 5-7 days a week, then go up to 10,000 if comfortable.
safety: Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness. If you have knee pain, heel pain or heart problems, get advice from a doctor first.

faq.q: Do I really need exactly 10,000 steps?
faq.a: No. 10,000 isn't a magic number. Consistently adding steps from where you are now matters more than chasing one number.

faq.q: How many calories do 1,000 steps burn?
faq.a: A rough estimate is 30-50 calories, depending on body weight and speed. It looks small, but it adds up every day.

faq.q: Is walking alone enough to lose weight?
faq.a: It's a great start. Combine it with suitable rice portions, more vegetables and protein, and strength training 2 times a week for more balanced results.
